input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only provision anywhere in the Agreement giving HDI a right to inspect our records (no other audit, verification or system-access right exists). It already satisfies two of the three fallback elements: 30 days' prior written notice (exceeding the 15-day fallback) and HDI bearing all inspection fees unconditionally (better than the fallback's "unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent"), and it is limited to normal business hours and to payment-calculation records. However, it contains no frequency limit, so HDI could inspect repeatedly and without limit, which fails the fallback (and approaches the walk-away "unlimited audits"). We therefore made the single minimal edit capping inspections at once per year, leaving the notice, business-hours and cost mechanics untouched. Preferred-only sub-elements (independent auditor, confidentiality undertaking, off-site conduct, 5% underpayment cost-shift) are noted but not pursued, as the clause otherwise sits at or above the fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accept HDI's inspection right, but our playbook requires a frequency cap, so we have limited it to once per year; the existing 30 days' written notice and HDI-borne costs already meet our position.
proposal.summary: Cap HDI's inspection right at once per year
